Unicode

04 - Unicode/5 - Unicode.md

If [[4 - Double Byte Character Set|DBCS]] was the messy, desperate hack to get Asian languages working on 8-bit systems Unicode is the clean, mathematically perfect reboot of the entire system of DBCS.

Unicode is a universal mapping standard. It is maintained by the Unicode Consortium, and its only job is to assign a unique, abstract ID number (called a “Code Point”) to every single character in human existence The C programming language as formalized by ANSI and inherently supports Unicode.

Unicode was initially only meant to assist ASCII and by any chance replace it, but then it became mainstream in today’s world.

Unicode is just a mapping of characters used by humans to some number or code, that means Unicode is also just a [[7 - Architecture of Text#Pillar 1 The Abstract Dictionary (Character Sets)|Character Set]] similar to [[1 - Early Character Encodings & The Rise of ASCII#ASCII|ASCII]] and the implementation of Unicode was done using [[6 - Wide Characters (The implementation of Unicode)|Wide Characters]] similar to how implementation of [[1 - Early Character Encodings & The Rise of ASCII#ASCII|ASCII]] in computer was done using [[3 - ANSI and Code Pages#The “ANSI” Character Set (Windows Latin 1)|ANSI]]

More details about [[6 - Wide Characters (The implementation of Unicode)|Wide Characters here]].
